name: IL-15
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans roughly 20 points Republican, one of the reddest seats in Illinois
Miller holds a roughly 9-to-1 fundraising edge as the incumbent ($1.8M vs. $200K raised)
No public polls or expert ratings; prediction markets price Miller at about 96%
A favorable national environment for Democrats narrows the margin but not the likely outcome
model.rationale: Miller is a heavy favorite given the district's 20-point Republican lean, her incumbency, and her dominant financial position; the national environment may trim the expected margin but poses little realistic threat to the result.
model.watch: Only an unusually large national Democratic wave, paired with major outside spending against Miller, could make this competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Illinois' 15th District is among the most Republican-leaning seats in the state, with a partisan lean of roughly 20 points toward the GOP. Incumbent Mary Miller, first elected in 2021, seeks another term with a large financial advantage, having raised about $1.8 million to Democrat Jennifer Todd's roughly $200,000. Outside spending has been minimal on both sides.

No public polls have surveyed the race, and national race raters have not issued ratings. Prediction markets price Miller's chances at roughly 96 percent. The national political environment appears favorable to Democrats, which narrows the expected margin somewhat, but the district's fundamentals remain heavily Republican. Miller is a strong favorite for re-election; Todd would need a historic swing well beyond anything recent cycles have produced in this territory.
